chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Feel of the 1940s Latin and jazz scene
summary: The bongo brought excitement that led to discotheques.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What about -- I'd like to move back now to the '40s again. We've talked about specific -- you talked last time about particular musicians that you played with. I'd like to try and get in, if you can cast your mind back to the feeling of what the jazz and the Latin scene was like, what you were playing at 52nd Street in Broadway. What were the clubs like? What kinds of people? Was it a very up scene?
During that era, was the revolution of music in the city. They were looking for something else. They

were looking for a (unintelligible) revolution. Anything. (Unintelligible.) The bongo created more excitement than they ever had before. And if you follow the pattern, that's where the discotheque come to be what it is today, because everything multiplied and multiplied and multiplied and multiplied into today.
Today, that music and the lights put the people in a frenzy. Never before there was that kind of excitement in music. So the Afro-Cubanists brought this.
